subject: Window ceiling & streaming qualification — Sanora discovery follow-up
messages:
From: Asha Raman <asha.raman@sanora.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@sanora.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T13:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + perf notes (Sanora)

Ben — thanks again for the demo today. A couple of clarifying items from our side so we can align internally: 1) Our main use case is a long-form summarization pipeline that ingests meeting transcripts (avg 6k tokens) and produces a structured 1–2k token summary with follow-up action bullets (streaming helpful). 2) Target latency is under 1s p95 for the user-facing summary page, but we can tolerate up to ~2s for batch backfill jobs. 3) Concurrent interactive users expected: 25 peak (early), with spikes to ~75 on demo days. 4) Expected sustained throughput: ~120 reqs/min (2 rps), but bursts up to ~300 rps for short windows when we onboard clients.

Can you confirm how your context-window options map to latency and whether prefix caching + streaming will preserve the sub-1s p95 target? Also, are there model variants you recommend for a 6k->2k workflow that reduce cost without sacrificing quality?

—Asha

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Raman <asha.raman@sanora.ai>
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@sanora.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-19T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + perf notes (Sanora)

Asha — great meeting, thanks for the clear write-up. High-level reactions and next steps below. TL;DR: sub-1s p95 for 6k->2k is achievable with streaming + dedicated capacity + prefix/KV caching, but requires tuned batching and either a quantized 16k model or a sharded 32k variant depending on quality needs.

Key points: 
- Context sizing: 6k input + 2k output fits inside 32k easily; 16k may work but leaves less headroom for internal tokens and tool-calls. 32k gives more flexibility for chains and safety prompts.
- Latency: For streaming, we look at token-emission latency (first token) and full-output latency. First-token latencies can be ~200–400ms on optimized GPU stacks; full 2k output will be dominated by token generation rate (~20–40ms/token depending on model/quant). Streaming allows UX to feel sub-1s because first token arrives quickly, but p95 on full-output will be larger.
- Concurrency/throughput: Your peak concurrent interactive users (75) with avg response lengths implies we should size for ~150 simultaneous model sessions (KV cache per session). That points to Dedicated pools with autoscale + burst.
- Cost/quality trade-offs: We can offer an int8/awq quantized 16k model for cost savings (~1.6–2x cheaper) with a small quality delta. For higher fidelity, an fp16 32k works but costs more.

Immediate next steps I propose: 1) Redwood to run a small bench (synthetic transcripts) to measure first-token and 95th latency across 16k-int8, 16k-fp16, and 32k-fp16 variants; 2) Sanora to share a 10–20 transcript sample and a priority prompt/template set; 3) agree on SLO targets (we recommend p95 first-token <= 350ms, p95 full-stream start <= 1.2s for interactive flows).

I'll loop in Dev to scope the bench run — Lauren will coordinate provisioning if Dedicated is required.

—Ben

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-21T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + perf notes (Sanora)

Ben / Lauren — I can own the perf bench. Notes on what I'll measure: 
- Cold vs warm session first-token latency (with/without KV cache).
- Per-token latency across token positions (to account for attention costs scaling with sequence length).
- Throughput curves (rps) with concurrency from 1 -> 300.
- Memory footprints and whether model sharding is needed for a 32k variant on our available GPU sizes.

I'll need: sample transcripts (10–20), expected prompt templates, and an example of the streaming client (so I can replicate initial chunk sizes). I'll provision a small Dedicated pool for the runs; cost estimate attached (see attachment stub).

—Dev

From: Asha Raman <asha.raman@sanora.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@sanora.ai>
Date: 2027-04-22T08:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + perf notes (Sanora)

Thanks — attaching the 12 sample transcripts and our canonical prompt templates (see Drive link as well). A few clarifications: 
- UX requirement is first meaningful token within 300–400ms; users tolerate streaming tokens after that.
- We prefer not to use heavy quantization if it noticeably affects summary coherence — willing to trade cost for quality up to a point.
- For spikes, we have a short-term mitigation: queueing UI + progressive loading, but we'd like backend buffering to keep tail latency reasonable.

Tom and I are available Wed/Thu to review the bench results.

—Asha

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Raman <asha.raman@sanora.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-25T09:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Window ceiling & streaming qualification — Sanora discovery follow-up

Quick recap and concrete commitments (per bench scope):
- Redwood action: Run bench across three model configs (16k-int8-awq, 16k-fp16, 32k-fp16) with their transcripts. Measure: first-token p50/p95, full-output p50/p95, per-token ms, memory/shard needs, and sustainable rps at target latency. Deliverable by 2027-04-29 EOD. (Owner: Dev)
- Sanora action: Confirm Drive link access and confirm if we should redact PII from transcripts (they look mostly sanitized). Provide any additional prompt variants by EOD 2027-04-26. (Owner: Asha)
- Recommended SLO proposal (suggested for contract): interactive-first-token p95 <= 350ms; interactive-full-stream start p95 <= 1.2s; sustained throughput SLA 150 rps with 5-min burst to 300 rps; concurrency guarantee: capacity for 150 active sessions with autoscale to 300 during bursts. (Owner: Ben / Lauren to include in Dedicated proposal)
- Fallbacks: If 16k-int8 quality is insufficient, we propose a hybrid rollout (canary on 16k-int8 for non-critical tenants + 32k-fp16 for premium customers) and prefix-based caching to serve repeated transcripts faster.

Next sync: bench results review on 2027-04-30 at 10:00am PT (tentative). I'll send calendar invite once Dev confirms runtime.

Best —
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
